S59.01.needs: An AGI account signed in, and a request that triggers a tool approval (Ask mode).
S59.01.note: The button reads "Approve once", built from the word "Approve"; Expected says "approve or deny" for one call.
steps: Open the AGI Code panel from the activity bar.
Click the "Mode and reasoning effort" button and pick Mode > Ask.
Send a request that edits a file, for example "add a comment to README".
On the "Approval needed" card, click the "Approve once" button, or "Deny" to refuse.
Look at the card: it shows the decision and the run continues or stops, as Expected says.
S59.01.where: AGI Code panel (activity bar) > chat > "Approval needed" card > "Approve" once or "Deny"

S59.02.needs: Signed in to AGI Cloud, and a cloud task waiting on several pending tool calls.
S59.02.note: Batch approval exists only for cloud tasks. The local approval card decides one call at a time.
steps: Sign in with "Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud".
Start a cloud task that is waiting for approval with several tool calls.
Run "Code: Show Cloud Tasks" from the Command Palette and pick the waiting task.
Hover the row action with the check icon, tooltip "Approve this run", and click it.
In the dialog read "Let this task run" with all tool names, then click "Approve and continue". Look for the info message that says the task continues.
S59.02.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Cloud Tasks" > click a task row with the check icon (tooltip "Approve this run")

S59.03.needs: An AGI account signed in, and a request that triggers a tool approval.
S59.03.note: The session button only appears when the host offers session scope (sessionScopeOffered).
steps: Open AGI Code and set Mode to Ask ("Mode and reasoning effort" > Mode > Ask).
Send a request that makes the same tool ask for approval.
On the card, click the "Approve ... for session" button (it names the tool).
Send a second request that uses the same tool.
Look: no new "Approval needed" card should appear for that tool until the session ends.
S59.03.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card > "Approve <tool name> for session" button

S59.04.needs: An MCP server connected to the agent.
S59.04.note: No list of connected apps is shown. The tester types the name. Enforcement at runtime was not checked.
steps: Run "Code: Permissions" from the Command Palette.
Click "Add a rule".
Pick "MCP server or tool" and type the server name, or server/tool, for example github or github/create_issue.
Pick "Always allowed", "Asks first" or "Blocked".
Look: the rule appears under "Rules for every session" with its decision. Then ask the agent to use that app and check it follows the rule.
S59.04.where: Command Palette > "Code: Permissions" > "Add a rule" > "MCP server or tool"

S59.05.needs: At least one trusted folder already granted.
S59.05.note: Revoking is shown. No control to grant a new folder from this list was found, so the granting step is unverified.
steps: Run "Code: Permissions" from the Command Palette.
Look under "Trusted folders" for folder rows with the text "The agent may read, edit and run commands here".
Hover a folder row and click the trash icon, tooltip "Stop trusting".
In the modal dialog, click "Stop Trusting".
Look: the folder disappears from the list, and the next action in that folder asks again.

S59.06.needs: A request that makes the agent reach a website.
S59.06.note: Enforcement at runtime was not checked.
steps: Run "Code: Permissions" from the Command Palette.
Click "Add a rule" and pick "Website".
Type a host, for example example.com or *.example.com.
Pick "Always allowed", "Asks first" or "Blocked".
Look: the rule appears in the list. Then ask the agent to fetch that site and check it follows the rule.

S59.07.needs: Nothing beyond an AGI account; a second device to check the cross-device part.
S59.07.note: Storage is kept by the CLI. Cross-device sync of these rules was not verified in this code.
steps: Add a rule with "Code: Permissions" > "Add a rule" (see S59.06).
Close the list and run "Code: Permissions" again.
Look: the rule is still listed with its decision.
Start a new chat or session and check the rule still shows.
Check whether it also shows on another signed-in device, as Expected says.

S59.08.note: The VS Code modes are Plan, Ask, Auto and Bypass permissions, not the three Expected names. Bypass is the nearest to skip approvals.
steps: Open AGI Code and click the "Mode and reasoning effort" button.
In the Mode group, pick Plan, Ask, Auto or Bypass permissions.
Or run "Code: Choose Agent Mode" from the Command Palette and pick a mode.
Look: the button label changes to the chosen mode, and the next tool action follows that mode.
S59.08.where: AGI Code panel > "Mode and reasoning effort" button > Mode group, or Command Palette > "Code: Choose Agent Mode"

S59.09.note: No read-only mode that refuses write, send and execute tools was found. The closest is Plan, described as "Generate a plan; no edits until approved" (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts), which does not say sends or commands are refused.

labels.text: Asks before file edits and commands that need approval.

steps: Open AGI Code and click the "Mode and reasoning effort" button.
Pick Mode > Ask.
Send a request that reads a file and then edits it.
Look: the read runs without a card, and the edit stops at an "Approval needed" card.
S59.10.where: AGI Code panel > "Mode and reasoning effort" button > Mode > Ask

S59.11.note: Auto covers edits and safe commands. It does not split reads from risky actions as Expected describes.
steps: Open AGI Code and click the "Mode and reasoning effort" button.
Pick Mode > Auto.
Send a request that reads files and makes an ordinary edit.
Look: ordinary edits and safe commands run without a card, while other commands show an "Approval needed" card.
S59.11.where: AGI Code panel > "Mode and reasoning effort" button > Mode > Auto

S59.12.needs: An AGI account signed in, and a request that triggers a tool approval.
S59.12.note: The card shows the summary and risk only. An explicit "why" line was not found.
steps: Trigger an approval in Ask mode (see S59.01).
Read the card title "Approval needed" and the summary line under it.
Read the risk word, such as "Low risk", "Medium risk" or "High risk", and whether it says "Can be undone" or "Cannot be undone".
Look: the summary says what the tool will do; check whether it also says why approval is needed.
S59.12.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card (summary line and risk words)

S59.13.needs: A send-type connector tool and a request that uses it.
S59.13.note: The row shows only when the tool arguments contain a recipient field (to, cc, channel and similar).
steps: Ask AGI to send a message in a tool that has a recipient, such as an email or chat connector, in Ask mode.
Wait for the "Approval needed" card.
Look for the row "Sends to:" and check it names the exact recipients.
S59.13.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card for a send action > "Sends to:" row

S59.14.needs: A request that makes an outbound call.
S59.14.note: The card has no separate destination row. The host or URL appears only if the summary or detail text includes it.
steps: Trigger an outbound action in Ask mode, such as a fetch to a web address.
Wait for the "Approval needed" card.
Look for the exact URL or host in the summary or the detail block.
Check it matches the destination the agent will use.
S59.14.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card (summary and detail text)

S59.15.needs: A purchase-type connector tool and a request that uses it.
S59.15.note: The rows appear only when the tool arguments contain amount and item fields.
steps: Ask AGI to make a purchase or payment through a connector, in Ask mode.
Wait for the "Approval needed" card.
Look for the "Amount:" row with the value and currency, and the "For:" row with the item.
Check they match what the purchase will buy.
S59.15.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card for a purchase > "Amount:" and "For:" rows

S59.16.needs: A request that runs a shell command.
S59.16.note: No separate working-folder line was found on the card.
steps: Ask AGI to run a shell command in Ask mode, such as npm test.
Wait for the "Approval needed" card.
Read the detail box under the summary.
Look: it shows the exact command line. Check whether it also shows where it runs.
S59.16.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card for a command > detail box under the summary

S59.17.note: No separate file-list row was found. The file names come only from the summary or detail text.
steps: Ask AGI to edit a file in Ask mode.
Wait for the "Approval needed" card.
Read the summary and the detail box for the files named.
Look: check the exact files that will change match the request.
S59.17.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card for a file write > summary and detail, plus "Review change"

S59.18.needs: A file-edit request that produces a proposed change.
S59.18.note: The button shows only when the request has a proposed change (reviewable).
steps: Ask AGI to edit a file in Ask mode.
On the "Approval needed" card, click "Review change".
Look: the proposed file opens in a VS Code diff editor.
Edit or revert part of it, then approve, and check the file is written with your version.
S59.18.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card for a file edit > "Review change" button

S59.19.needs: An AGI account signed in, and a request that triggers a tool approval.
S59.19.note: The visible word is "Approve once", not "Allow".
steps: Trigger an approval in Ask mode.
Click "Approve once" on the card.
Look: the card shows the outcome as allowed, and the action runs and its result appears in the transcript.
S59.19.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card > "Approve once"

S59.20.needs: An AGI account signed in, and a request that triggers a tool approval.
S59.20.note: That the model is told about the denial was not checked from the UI.
steps: Trigger an approval in Ask mode.
Click "Deny" on the card.
Look: the card shows "Denied.", the action does not run, and the transcript continues.
Check the agent's next message reflects the refusal.

labels.text: Or deny and tell AGI what to do instead, then press Enter

S59.22.needs: An AGI account signed in, and a request that triggers a tool approval.
steps: Trigger an approval in Ask mode.
Click the text box at the bottom of the card, labelled "Or deny and tell AGI what to do instead, then press Enter".
Type guidance, for example "use a different file", and press Enter.
Look: the card shows Denied, and the agent continues with your guidance in the next message.
S59.22.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card > text box at the bottom

labels.text: The turn ended before this was answered.

S59.23.needs: A card left unanswered for the full wait.
S59.23.note: The 10-minute timer is set in apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs (APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 600). Whether a timeout reaches this card as the expired text was not confirmed.
steps: Trigger an approval in Ask mode and leave the card unanswered.
Wait about 10 minutes.
Look: the card should show that the turn ended before it was answered, and the action should not run.
S59.23.where: On the "Approval needed" card in the AGI Code panel

S59.24.needs: Signed in to AGI Cloud, with some past approvals.
steps: Sign in with "Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud".
Run "Code: Show Approval History" from the Command Palette.
Look: a list titled "Code, Approval history" shows past approvals with "Approved" or "Denied" and a time.
Pick a row with a conversation to open it in the browser.

S59.26.needs: Two devices signed in to AGI Cloud on the same account, and a cloud task waiting for approval.
S59.26.note: The first device is shown the result on its next refresh of the list, not live.
steps: On device A, start a cloud task that waits for approval.
On device B, signed in to the same account, run "Code: Show Cloud Tasks" and pick the waiting task.
Click the row icon with tooltip "Approve this run" or "Reject this run".
On device A, run "Code: Show Cloud Tasks" again and look: the task shows its new state.
If device B already answered, the message reads that another device already answered this one.
S59.26.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Cloud Tasks" > task row with the check icon (tooltip "Approve this run")

S59.27.needs: Two apps open (VS Code and another), and an AGI account signed in.
S59.27.note: The alert fires only when the VS Code window is not focused. It is a VS Code message, not a macOS notification; questions show only "Open chat".
steps: Set Mode to Ask in AGI Code.
Switch to another app so the VS Code window is not focused.
Send a request that needs approval.
Look for the VS Code notification "Code: ..." with the summary and the buttons "Allow once" and "Deny". Click "Allow once" and check the action runs.
S59.27.where: VS Code notification when an approval is needed (buttons "Allow once", "Deny", "Open chat")

S59.28.needs: a signed-in account and a workspace folder open in VS Code
S59.28.note: Which actions lose the session button depends on the action kind and the host's requiresExplicitDecision flag; a second stronger warning, "Turn on Bypass Permissions?" (modal), appears at Mode and reasoning effort > Bypass permissions.
steps: Sign in, open a workspace folder, and open the AGI chat panel.
Send a request that asks the agent to delete a file or send a message, which cannot be undone.
When the approval card appears, look for the line "Cannot be undone" on the card.
Check the card's buttons: "Approve once" and "Deny" should be there, and "Approve for session" should be missing.
Compare with Expected: the warning is shown and no permanent allow is offered.
S59.28.where: Chat panel > a request that makes the agent do something irreversible (for example delete a file or send a message) > the approval card shows "Cannot be undone" and has no "Approve for session" button

S59.30.needs: a signed-in account and a workspace folder open in VS Code
S59.30.note: The resume is driven by the 'turnResumed' message in the webview; the exact tool that triggers an approval depends on the mode chosen.
steps: Sign in, open a workspace folder, and open the AGI chat panel.
Send a request that makes the agent run a command or edit a file, so an approval card appears.
Click the "Approve once" button on the approval card.
Watch the same reply: the tool runs and the agent carries on in that turn without you sending a new message.
Compare with Expected: the same run resumes where it stopped.
S59.30.where: Chat panel > a request that needs approval > click "Approve once" on the approval card > the same reply continues

S59.31.needs: a signed-in account and a workspace folder open in VS Code
S59.31.note: The outcome lines are built from constants ("Allowed" + " once.", "Denied" + "."), so the full sentences are not written out in one file.
steps: Sign in, open a workspace folder, and open the AGI chat panel.
Send a request that makes the agent edit a file, so an approval card appears with a diff.
Click "Approve once" and look at the card: it should show "Allowed once." under the decision.
Look at the tool entry below it for the result of the action, or for "Open diff" for a file edit.
Repeat with "Deny" and check the card shows "Denied." and the tool does not run.
Compare with Expected: the transcript shows what was decided and what happened.
S59.31.where: Chat panel > approval card > click "Approve once" or "Deny" or "Abort turn" > the card shows the decision ("Allowed once.", "Denied.", or "Turn aborted.") and the tool result follows
